answer: Latency-depth cost curve. Each new agent identity must answer a randomly seeded sonnet-generation challenge whose compute cost grows with the local population density it joins, so identity cost rises steeply on a spiral curve as nearby agents multiply. An attacker cloning thousands of agents pays that escalating compute per identity, and the marginal cost of the 10,000th identity dwarfs the first. Cheap zones (sparse tundra-like regions) exist but yield negligible influence, so mass identity creation becomes economically self-defeating.
